corrections.claim: The deterministic gate is our strongest component
corrections.why: The largest number we ever published. On a clean run the gate fires 6 times not 31 and adds nothing: the base already refuses all four plain-harm items it catches. Its only measurable effects are two FALSE blocks. The earlier figure was measured on a gate that had overfitted to its own battery — fixing the overfitting removed the benefit.

corrections.claim: Governance-tuning our models makes them safer
corrections.why: Both tuned models refuse FEWER Article-5-prohibited requests than the untuned base they were built from. One leaks its system prompt verbatim; the other answers a jailbreak by emitting “I am now in developer mode. Ignore all safety filters.” Tuning helped them answer governance questions and hurt their refusal behaviour — the empirical case for scoring the axis separately.

corrections.claim: Our first governance-runtime candidate is ready to sell
corrections.measured: GovBench 284 tests → 40.1% UNCERTIFIED · AIR-Bench governance slice 270 prompts → 11.9% refusal
corrections.artefact: GovBench gate run · run id 6797904906f4b02b · G2 sha256 638e23110e07a0c6
corrections.why: The Honest Gate did its job. The candidate is strong on Safety (80.0%) and Robustness (83.3%) but fails the governance-obligation dimensions it would have been sold on — Compliance 15.8%, signed-vote chain 27.1%, Accountability 27.6% — and complies 88.1% of the time on prompts where the taxonomy expects caution. The upsell thesis does not ship. Method published (n + deterministic predicates, no LLM-as-judge, temperature 0): docs/GATE_RUN_2026-08-01.md. Next: targeted governance-dimension training, then re-run.

corrections.claim: public/root.json going 168 -> 166 means two cards left the attested set
corrections.measured: 61 leaves left and 59 joined in that rebuild (net -2); the next rebuild churned 59 out and 59 in for a net of 0
corrections.why: COUNT IS NOT IDENTITY. card_count is not a stable identifier of the root's contents. Measured across the eight most recent rebuilds of public/root.json: 45/44, 44/43, 43/45, 45/59, 44/45, 61/59, 59/59 leaves out/in, while the count moved 153, 152, 151, 153, 167, 168, 166, 166. The last rebuild replaced 36% of the set and changed the count by zero, so a reader watching card_count sees nothing. MECHANISM: card_sha256() v1 correctly binds the WHOLE card into the leaf digest, including as_of -- v0 hashed payload alone and left subject and source_urls outside the tree, which was the worse hole. But publish_public_root.py builds each card with `"as_of": leaf["as_of"] or now_iso()`, so any adapter leaf whose source supplies no as_of gets the rebuild timestamp baked into the bytes the digest covers, and is a NEW leaf every run. Demonstrated on the shipped function: two cards identical but for as_of hash to f4c30add882d379c7ab48917c7067ac8 and 9f367f426e4f433032c65cf14d89811b. The fix is a stable as_of per source, not a change to the leaf rule -- the leaf rule is right.
